notes:
Summary: NorthStar builds a cloud-first contact center orchestration layer used by e-commerce & telecom customers. Primary goal is reliable agent-assist + reranking under heavy bursts (Black Friday-style and major outages). They need predictable degradation (graceful fallbacks), <500ms agent suggestion end-to-end during normal traffic, and acceptable p95 routing decision latency <150ms. Current environment: hybrid (private cloud + colos).

Key pain: seasonal peaks and incident bursts cause long queue depths and cascading failures — they currently throttle upstream LLMs which produces junk suggestions; want gating and degraded-mode UX rather than full failure. Quote from CTO: "If our LLM layer trips during peak, ops teams get buried — we need graceful degradation, not a pileup."

Requirements (customer stated):
- Workloads: real-time agent assist, automated ticket summarization post-call, tool-calling for CTS (CRM updates)
- Spike profile: baseline 6k concurrent channels, sustained campaign peaks to 28-40k concurrent for 90-120 minutes; occasional 6–8x microbursts lasting 30–90s
- SLOs: p50 suggestion latency <200ms, p95 suggestion latency <500ms (normal); p95 routing decision <150ms always; error rate <0.5% after fallbacks
- Throughput targets: support 10k tokens/sec average during peak windows, scale to 35k tokens/sec in burst mode without >30% increase in tail latency
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; want optimize recommendations to balance quantization vs quality for agent assist (no >6% quality degradation allowed)
technical_notes: Pilot scope: Dedicated pool + autoscale policies, prefix/KV cache enabled, prefix-based caching for common templates
Spike test plan: synthetic traffic generator that simulates 6k -> 40k concurrent channels over 2-hour window; inject microbursts and long tail slowdowns
Fallback strategy requested: model-variant downgrade, response-summarization (short form), and routing to local cached templates when KV cache hit
Observability asks: token-level cost, per-route p95/p99 latency, queue depth, autoscaler provision time, cold-start counts
Security: require customer KMS + SAML SSO; data residency for EU customers (some tenants), audit logs retained 13 months
poc_details: 6-week pilot: week1 onboarding, week2 integration + small footprint, week3 stress test dry-run, week4 full spike test, week5 tuning (quantization & batching), week6 final report
Success criteria: pass spike test with p95 latencies within targets OR graceful degradation with controlled QoS loss; acceptable per-token cost delta vs baseline
SLA asks: <2 min failover to fallback routing; autoscaler target: add 2 GPU nodes within 90-120s during microbursts
procurement_notes: Revenue motion likely reserved capacity (Dedicated) + Optimize package. Legal requested KMS addendum; procurement expects decision after spike report and SOC2 docs.
